newsitem.title: USA: Wet week stalls Montana fieldwork, plantings lag.
newsitem.headline: Wet week stalls Montana fieldwork, plantings lag.

text.p: A wet week stalled fieldwork in the week ending Sunday, pushing sugarbeet and corn plantings further behind average, Montana's agricultural statistics service said in its weekly crop update.
Sugarbeets were 25 percent planted, against the five-year average of 47 percent. Corn was two percent planted, compared with the 15 percent average.
Winter damage to the winter wheat crop was rated 36 percent light, 13 percent moderate and one percent heavy.
Freeze damage was rated 58 percent none, 30 percent light, nine percent moderate and three percent heavy.
Winter wheat conditions were rated one percent very poor, six percent poor, 33 percent fair, 55 percent good and five percent excellent.
Topsoil moisture was rated mostly adequate to surplus, with four percent rated short.

Livestock conditions were mixed. Areas in the east reported higher death losses due to cold temperatures and poor quality and quantity of feed available for cattle. Ranchers in some counties were very short of feed, the report said.
Nine percent of cattle and calves had been moved to summer ranges. Calving was 90 percent complete.
